question: Should OpenClaw support the new public `api.registerReadinessCriterion` Plugin SDK contract and `gateway.readiness` selector configuration as a V1 compatibility commitment?
rationale: The callback, selector IDs, timeout behavior, and readiness admission semantics become a supported external contract; code review cannot determine whether that product and maintenance commitment is desired.

options.title: Approve the V1 readiness contract
options.body: Keep the public plugin registration API and operator-selected criteria, then require exact-head compatibility and live recovery proof before merge.

options.title: Land core-only observations first
options.body: Defer plugin registration and keep the implementation limited to core-owned readiness facts until a Plugin SDK contract is separately approved.

options.title: Pause the readiness stack
options.body: Defer this feature until the RFC and ownership model receive explicit maintainer sponsorship.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 readiness contract
recommendation.body: Keep the public plugin registration API and operator-selected criteria, then require exact-head compatibility and live recovery proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the related readiness-stack proposals and can provide the clearest implementation and RFC context, though final acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
